source.title: GPT and Prejudice: A Sparse Approach to Understanding Learned Representations in Large Language Models

page_placements.theme: Feature roles and specialization vary with depth and model scale

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether concept-selective sparse features can be recovered from a language model using SAEs, bearing on V4 with a different method from the original toy-model experiments. It does not test the original toy-model geometry or capacity mechanism.
record.gate_note: Relevant results are the study's own SAE feature-to-concept mappings and detector statistics. Perplexity, SAE reconstruction metrics, cited findings from other work, and the study's descriptions of its method are not recorded as claim-result rows.
record.test_reason: The study assumes SAEs resolve superposition and uses them as an instrument to audit corpus themes. It reports only its own pipeline's concept-mapping outputs, with no control. There is no comparison with dense neurons, random or shuffled features, or the chance AP implied by label prevalence. So its numbers cannot show whether the model contains sparse features an SAE recovers beyond what any projection would give. The authors frame the work as corpus analysis, not as a test of superposition or SAE recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors present LLM+SAE probing as a proof-of-concept, scalable framework for surfacing the thematic and cultural structures (a gender–family–marriage backbone) a model absorbs from its training corpus. They acknowledge that results depend on the 11 chosen concepts and the probing prompts. They do not claim to test superposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a custom GPT-style transformer trained on nineteenth-century novels, then trains top-k SAEs and maps their activations to curated concept labels. It does not reproduce the original toy-model feature-learning setup or measure its sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported associations depend on the selected 11 concepts and 665 curated prompts. The number of selective SAE neurons and their associations vary across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE units in deeper layers are more entangled across concepts. Mean polarity falls from 0.407 at layer 2 to about 0.22 at layers 7–8. The primary–secondary AP gap shrinks from 0.135 at layer 2 to 0.068 at layer 8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents in deeper layers of a small LM are less concept-specific (more polysemantic with respect to human labels) than in earlier layers.

record.problems: Evidence comes from one custom model trained on about 7.6 million tokens of a curated literary corpus, and from 665 curated prompts annotated for 11 chosen concepts. The paper notes that results depend on the probing dataset and that some categories are difficult to capture. No uncertainty estimates or explicit control comparisons are reported. SAE reconstruction MSE increases with depth, although those reconstruction metrics are not claim-result rows here.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported claim-relevant feature-mapping results were left out. SAE reconstruction metrics and language-model perplexity were excluded because they do not measure the feature-to-concept recovery named by V4.

untested.parts: All: no toy model, no geometry, no sparsity transition.
All: no test that capacity competition causes polysemanticity.
Whether SAE features recover sparse features beyond baseline. No dense-neuron or random-direction control, and no chance AP is reported.
All: no completeness, stability or canonicality tests.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V4 labels are not justified. Each 'supports' rests on top-ranked units without a baseline, and each 'limits_scope' rests on probe-dependent aggregates. The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only as background motivation for using SAEs. Neuron ID 2130 in layers 3 and 4 belongs to different SAEs, so it is not the same unit.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, near-orthogonal geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry.
The study does not test whether feature competition for limited capacity causes polysemanticity, or whether important features obtain dedicated dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemanticity arises independently of capacity pressure or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The study analyzes one custom GPT-style model trained on a small literary corpus, not commercial or larger LLMs. Its SAE features are associated with a selected set of 11 concepts using curated prompts; it does not establish feature recovery across broader concepts or settings.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
The study does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: custom GPT-style model
rows.size_stated: 896-dimensional token embeddings; 8 Transformer Blocks; parameter count not stated
rows.stage_stated: trained only for next-token generation; not instruction fine-tuned
rows.operation_detail: Mapped SAE activations to labeled concepts and reported layer-wise selective-neuron counts, mean primary AP, and mean polarity.
rows.measure: Selective neurons: 4; mean primary AP: 0.223; mean polarity: 0.127.
rows.note: Layer-wise statistics from the study's concept-probing analysis.
rows.check: These are layer-wise counts of SAE units passing the authors' own selectivity filter, plus mean AP and polarity. The count depends on the filter thresholds and on SAE width, which grows with depth (×3 to ×5). Mean AP of 0.22–0.27 has no chance baseline, so it cannot be read as V4 recovery. Values match Table 3A.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Assumes SAEs disentangle superposed representations and applies them as an instrument for corpus analysis, without a comparison establishing superposition or dictionary completeness.

tranche.reason: Uses SAEs to map corpus themes and reports pipeline outputs; it does not independently test a superposition claim version (§§2.2, 5–8).

source_check.notes: Exact mean polarities are 0.220 at Layer 7 and 0.230 at Layer 8; the statement's approximation is reasonable. Selective-unit counts depend on the probing labels and filters, with SAE width also increasing across depth.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The listed top SAE detector neurons
reader_labels.reason: Several SAE units have AP values from 0.56 to 0.74 for their primary concept, including detectors with no secondary concept (r15-r21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layer-wise and concept-level aggregates in the single custom model
reader_labels.reason: The study reports many selective SAE units, but mean primary AP is 0.222–0.265 by layer, and category counts and selectivity vary; some categories are weak or rare (r1-r14, r22-r24).
